links.why: R1: 'And God said' introduces what is said, 'Let there be light'. The saying clause links to the said clause as well as the turn's frame and part.
Direction reversed. The narrative runs from the saying clause (cl0) to the clause after it (cl2); 'it was light' follows 'God said', it does not precede it.
cl1 is inside the speech, and the narrative line does not continue from inside a speech. What came of the command is recorded as its result instead.
wayyiqtol cl2 continues the narrative line from the nearest clause before it that is not inside a speech, the saying clause cl0.
A jussive command, then waw + wayyiqtol saying what came of it ('and it was light'). This is the effect of imp1.

groups.why: God is the speaker ('God said'). The turn holds the saying as frame and the commanded words as part.
'part' is not a member role of the imperative kind. cl2, 'and it was light', is what the command brings about, so it is the group's effect.

cant_tell.why: The text names no one to whom God says 'let there be light'; the words are a jussive with no named addressee.
